tools.description: Simulates the cron: GET on /in/:id. No credential on purpose — the caller is a cron, and the ID is already the secret.

tools.description: Says the run STARTED. Does not clear the dead-man clock: a routine that starts and hangs still becomes a miss. tools.name: signal_fail
tools.description: Record a failed run. The next five-minute check sends the alert with reason fail. The monitor's alert_repeat_sec controls repeated alerts; the default is 24 hours. Failing is not proof of life either: the clock keeps running. The ingest never sends e-mail and never calls out — it records `alert_pend

tools.name: signal_exit_code
tools.description: The shell exit status: 0 behaves like a ping, 1-255 record the code as a failure. `curl -fsS $ORIGIN/in/ID/$?` at the end of a script is the whole integration. `0` behaves exactly like a plain ping; 1 to 255 record the code and leave the failure for the cron.

tools.name: ingest_key
tools.description: Returns (minting the first time) the key for /in/<key>/<slug>, where a ping creates its own monitor inside the free tier. Instruments a whole fleet with no setup call per job. One key per owner. The key survives signing in: the crontab you deployed keeps working.

tools.name: ingest_key_rotate
tools.description: Rotates the ingest key; the previous one stops creating monitors. Existing ones keep working. Monitors already created keep working — rotating only revokes the power to create new ones.

tools.name: ping_slug
tools.description: Create a monitor on its first check-in. The same slug uses the same monitor. A rejected creation writes no monitor or event. The slug becomes the monitor name and its identity: the same slug always means the same monitor, so a retry never creates a second one. Normalised to lowercase, `[a-z0-9-]`, 4

tools.name: signal_slug
tools.description: Send start, fail or an exit code by name, with the ingest key; the first signal of a new name creates its monitor. tools.name: status_feed_url
tools.description: Public URL (JSON and RSS) with the status of all the owner's endpoints. The feed token only reads status: it does not create, change or delete. Whoever has the link sees the dashboard — treat it as a secret.

tools.name: status_feed_rotate
tools.description: Rotates the status feed token; the previous URL stops working.

tools.name: list_templates
tools.description: Ingest snippets and the JSON HookPulse POSTs on a miss. It exists so nobody guesses the alert format: `miss_json` and `recovery_json` here are the same bodies that arrive at your `alert_url`. Slack and Discord receive only the field they read.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_endpoint, create_site, import_crontab, signal_start, signal_fail, ping_slug, list_templates, contact · Private data: create_guest, create_endpoint, create_site, import_crontab, get_endpoint, ping_ingest, signal_start, signal_fail, signal_exit_code, status_feed_url, status_feed_rotate, contact · Public sink: create_endpoint, create_site, import_crontab, signal_start, signal_fail, ping_slug, signal_slug, contact · Destructive: create_endpoint, create_site, get_endpoint, delete_endpoint, signal_start, signal_fail, status_feed_url, list_templates.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_endpoint, create_site, import_crontab, signal_start, signal_fail, ping_slug, list_templates, contact · Private data: create_guest, create_endpoint, create_site, import_crontab, get_endpoint, ping_ingest, signal_start, signal_fail, signal_exit_code, status_feed_url, status_feed_rotate, contact · Public sink: create_endpoint, create_site, import_crontab, signal_start, signal_fail, ping_slug, signal_slug, contact · Destructive: create_endpoint, create_site, get_endpoint, delete_endpoint, signal_start, signal_fail, status_feed_url, list_templates

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
